root_cause: The Escape keydown listener in dialog-base.ts early-returns for modal dialogs, relying solely on the native cancel event to prevent dialog closure. After multiple Escape presses, the cancel listener fails to preventDefault, causing the dialog to close unexpectedly.
repair_strategy: Modify the Escape keydown listener to explicitly handle modal dialogs when keyboard: false by preventing default and triggering the backdrop transition, while preserving existing behavior for modal dialogs with keyboard: true and non‑modal dialogs.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will no longer dismiss the confirmation dialog when opened with keyboard: false, allowing users to press Escape repeatedly without losing focus or closing the dialog, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (keyboard) and 2.4.3 (focus order).
functional_risks: Modal dialogs with keyboard: true will continue to close on Escape via the existing cancel listener (unchanged).
Non‑modal dialogs with keyboard: false will remain unaffected (Escape does nothing).
If keyboard: false is set incorrectly, the backdrop transition may be triggered, but this matches the static backdrop behavior.
No changes to the Cancel transfer or Send buttons; they retain their existing functionality.
verification_requirements: Press Escape any number of times on the confirmation dialog; the dialog must remain open and focus must stay in the OTP field.
Press Escape on the help dialog; it must close as before.
Press Escape on a non‑modal dialog with keyboard: true; it must close.
Confirm that the Cancel transfer button still closes the dialog and sets status to 'Cancelled'.
Confirm that entering a six‑digit code and pressing Send sends the transfer and closes the dialog.
